PullRequest.Title: agentHost: anchor Copilot customizations to each chat's own folders
PullRequest.Body:

## Bug

A Copilot peer chat in a multi-folder session gets the wrong folder's customizations. A peer working in the session's second folder discovered the first folder's agents, instructions, skills and workspace MCP servers (multi-root off), or the union of all folders (multi-root on), because discovery was anchored to the session rather than to the chat. After a chat-only move, the default chat also kept discovering from its previous folder. Claude and Codex already discover from the chat's own folder.

## Fix (Copilot only, no protocol change, no Claude/Codex change)

The fix follows the agreed design for per-chat Copilot customization anchors (Copilot provider only).

- **Per-chat anchors.** A chat's customization anchors are its own effective working directories: its first, plus its others only when Copilot multi-root is enabled. A fork anchors to its own folder, and a worktree-isolated chat to its worktree. Workspace-less and provisional sessions are unchanged.
- **Discovery split from the session's active client.** On-disk discovery (agents, skills, instructions, workspace MCP config) moves into refcounted `CustomizationAnchor`s, one per ordered anchor set, owned by the session's `SessionPluginController`. Chats in the same folder share one, a set is never discovered twice, and a set is released with the last chat using it and on session finalize. The session's `ActiveClient` keeps the client tool set and client-synced plugins, so client updates still reach every chat. A chat's SDK snapshot is its anchor set's discoveries plus the session's client contributions.
- **Published view = default chat.** `SessionState.customizations` stays the default chat's list. It follows a chat-only move of the default chat (no enablement rebase, no project change) and keeps publishing discovery changes after any reanchor.
- **Older builds.** `copilot.sharedCustomizationDirectories` is still written exactly as before, but this build no longer reads it, either in the provider or in the host's session-settings derivation (`agentChatContext.ts`, consumed only by Copilot).
- **Agent picker fallback.** Agent pickers list the session's published (default chat) agents. When a chat's selected custom agent isn't discovered by its own anchor set, that one agent is taken from the published anchor set, at create, materialize, resume and send. Instructions and skills stay the chat's own folder's.
- **One folder, one key.** Anchor-set keys use the comparison keys of the folders' real paths, so a folder reached as `/tmp/...` and `/private/tmp/...` (or through another symlink or casing) is one anchor set. The paths passed to the SDK are unchanged.

## Decisions and known limitations

- MCP runtime state publishing is unchanged: every live chat still publishes MCP state to the session list, and the last writer wins (pre-existing). With per-folder anchors, a peer's folder-only MCP servers also appear in the session list. Per-chat customization state is planned separately. A test pins this behaviour.
- Pre-existing, not changed here (reproduced on `main`):
  - The Agents window drops an existing peer's agent selection from the turn message.
  - The workspace-move continuation turn clears the chat's custom agent.
  - With multi-root off, a peer can't change folder once a session has more than one chat. This is a deliberate gate.

## How to test

Use two folders, each with its own `.github/agents/*.agent.md` and `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`.

1. In the Agents window, create a session in folder 1 and send a message. The reply follows folder 1's instructions.
2. Open a nested chat (Cmd+T) and move it to folder 2 with `set_workspace`. Its replies follow folder 2's instructions only, with multi-root on and off.
3. Move the default chat chat-only to folder 2. Its next reply follows folder 2, and the agent picker lists folder 2's agent.

## Validation

All runs were made with `COPILOT_*`, `AGENT_HOST_*` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` unset, at the PR head on top of main (after #341626 merged).

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck-client` | ✅ clean |
| `npm run eslint -- <5 changed .ts files>` | ✅ clean |
| `npm run valid-layers-check` | ✅ passed (before the final rebase; no import changes since) |
| `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run .../copilotAgentSession.test.ts --run .../agentHostSeams.test.ts --run .../agentHostSessionStateOwnershipGuard.test.ts` | ✅ 1838 passing, 1 pending |
| `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts` (strict replay) | ✅ 268 passing, 24 pending, exit 0 |
| `./scripts/test.sh --grep "AgentHost\|Chat"` | ✅ 12652 passing, 70 pending, 1 failing before the final rebases. The failure is a load-sensitive timing flake in `AgentHostChatContributions` "clears automatic archive time…", in code this PR doesn't touch; 15/15 runs passed when quiet. #341626 (now on main) rewrote that test to await the store. |
| Mutation checks (each rule's test fails with the rule reverted) | ✅ 17 mutations, all caught |
| Live, Agents window, Claude Sonnet 5.5, two folders with distinct agents and instructions | ✅ peer in folder 2 → folder 2 only (multi-root on and off); default chat unchanged; default chat follows its chat-only move; peer picker lists the session's agents |

New tests in `copilotAgent.test.ts` (suite "per-chat customization anchors"):
- the peer in folder 2 gets folder 2's agents, instructions and MCP servers (multi-root off and on);
- the default chat follows a chat-only move;
- the published view republishes after a move and after a restart;
- the published view stays the default chat's when a peer starts first;
- chats share one discovery per folder, including across folder spellings;
- client tools reach every chat;
- anchors are released with their last chat and on session finalize;
- a read during teardown is safe;
- the selected-agent fallback works;
- a peer's folder-only MCP server appears in the session list.

`agentHostSeams.test.ts` covers the host settings derivation.

**Not run:** the broad `AgentHost|Chat` suite after the final rebases; the cross-platform Azure pipeline; the Claude and Codex E2E suites, since no Claude or Codex code changed. The selected-agent fallback couldn't be exercised live, because of the pre-existing client issue above; unit tests and mutations cover it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a default Copilot chat and send turns in its existing folder set
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cold launch/resume must resolve file-path identities, settle customization discovery, read workspace MCP configuration, and build the SDK snapshot before session creation can proceed. Ordinary warm sends still read stored working-directory metadata, but reuse the live anchor's settled discovery; the new realpath lookup is served from the session map and MCP refresh returns its initialized snapshot.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each file-backed anchor directory with fs.realpath for identity normalization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per distinct successful path spelling per session; warm turns have zero filesystem calls from this step because _realPaths is populated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No real-path normalization was performed for customization discovery anchors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold launch/resume waits for path resolution before acquiring the anchor; warm sends do not cross this boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request agent, instruction, and skill discovery paths and discovered items from the Copilot SDK.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six SDK RPCs for a cold effective anchor; zero additional RPCs on warm turns until a watched change triggers refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery RPC set ran once for the session-wide discovery anchor; for the default chat's unchanged folder set the call count remains one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold snapshot creation waits for discovery; warm sends reuse the settled anchor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve customization directories/files, install file watchers, parse discovered files, and read each root's .mcp.json.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Initial work is once per cold customization anchor; MCP root scans/watchers are additionally shared by root through acquireRootMcpDiscovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent filesystem discovery existed on the single session anchor; the PR changes ownership to refcounted per-folder-set anchors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold snapshot waits for initial discovery and MCP refresh; subsequent refreshes are watcher-driven.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read persisted working-directory metadata during send configuration refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata read per send/resume/start-MCP operation, independent of anchor count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This per-operation metadata read already existed and its frequency is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It is awaited in parallel with snapshot construction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective cardinality is one customization anchor per ordered set of real-path-normalized working directories, not per turn or per chat when chats share that set. Multi-root discovery scales with the roots in that set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery's SDK calls and filesystem work use Promise.all within one cold anchor. Session operations are generally session-queued; live references coalesce chats on the same anchor. No new unbounded limiter bypass was established.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold anchors resolve each file path once and initialize discovery once. Warm snapshots await settled promises and reuse cached real paths, parsed customization state, MCP root discovery, and watchers. Failed realpath resolutions are retried, but the single lookup per operation on a missing folder did not establish a meaningful regression on a viable chat workflow.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path, cache keys, and boundary counts from the changed acquisition path and transitive discovery implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold discovery duration depends on SDK process latency, filesystem size, and root count. The mechanism is bounded and warm behavior is clear; no evidence showed a disproportionate new cost for the unchanged default-chat scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added realpath boundary is one-time for successful paths, while the existing expensive discovery remains coalesced for the effective anchor and reused on warm sends.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create peer chats in different folders or folder combinations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each peer's first create/materialize/resume must acquire its own folder-set anchor and settle its SDK/filesystem customization discovery before constructing the peer SDK snapshot. Later sends reuse the live chat entry's anchor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve peer folder real paths for anchor-key coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful realpath per unique spelling per session; shared peers do not repeat it after the map is warm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Peers reused the session-wide discovery and did not resolve a peer-specific customization anchor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Peer creation waits for resolution before discovery can be shared.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run Copilot SDK customization discovery for the peer's projectPaths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six RPCs per cold effective anchor set, shared across every chat using that set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All peers reused the one session discovery, so a peer in another folder did not cause a separate SDK discovery pass but also received the wrong folder's customizations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Peer snapshot creation waits for the cold discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan and parse customization files and establish watchers for the peer anchor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per distinct live anchor set, then watcher-driven. Shared folder sets perform one pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the session anchor was scanned; peer-specific folders were not correctly discovered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold peer creation waits; warm peer turns do not rescan.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and watch .mcp.json for peer roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RootMcpDiscovery per file-service/root even when several anchor sets include that root; SessionMcpDiscovery only merges root snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only roots in the session-wide anchor were reached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold peer snapshot waits for initial root refresh.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost grows with the number of distinct simultaneously used ordered anchor sets after real-path normalization, not raw chat count. Multiple chats in the same folder set share one discovery. Different sets can overlap roots, but MCP root I/O/watchers are shared independently.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Normal peer creation is session-queued. Independent fork queues can overlap cold anchors, but no evidence established a realistic unbounded burst; each anchor itself runs a fixed group of discovery operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Positive anchor entries are refcounted and shared by normalized key. Chats in the same folder set hit the warm anchor. Anchor state is dropped with the last user, so later reuse correctly performs a fresh scan rather than retaining stale watchers indefinitely. Symlink spellings are normalized before acquisition and live entries are rekeyed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that boundary work scales with distinct anchors and that same-set chats coalesce, based on acquireAnchor refcounts, real-path keys, and tests asserting one discovery.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions with many distinct folder combinations can perform more cold discovery than before, and exact SDK/filesystem duration is environment-dependent. However, this is the required work to produce distinct authoritative folder-scoped snapshots, is keyed by effective sets, and is released when unused; no redundant per-chat repetition was proven.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The increased cold work is causally tied to correcting per-folder discovery and is bounded/coalesced at the strongest safe key shown by the APIs; reporting it would be generic optimization advice rather than an actionable regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move the default chat to another folder and publish the new customization view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The move transaction updates provider state and persisted metadata. Publishing the new view starts asynchronously via publishWhenSettled and is off the move's awaited critical path; the next send awaits the new anchor snapshot if discovery is still cold.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover the destination folder's customizations and MCP configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold discovery for the destination anchor; zero if an existing peer already holds the same set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A chat-only default move kept discovery on the old shared roots and did not scan the destination for the published view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publication is fire-and-forget from the move; a subsequent send may wait for completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist working-directory metadata and backward-compatible shared roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The move already persisted working-directory and shared-root metadata; the PR changes which roots current builds read, not the transaction frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence remains awaited by the move transaction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One new cold anchor for the moved-to ordered folder set unless a peer already holds it. Repeated moves reuse any still-live matching anchor; otherwise released sets are rediscovered when legitimately revisited.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The move is serialized by the existing working-directory transaction. Discovery internals parallelize fixed categories, while publication waits on the single effective anchor.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reanchor clears only the published reference. If another chat holds the destination anchor, publication and relaunch share its settled discovery. The old anchor remains only while another live chat needs it and otherwise disposes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the reanchor, refcount, and publishWhenSettled paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Destination discovery latency varies by filesystem and customization volume, but it occurs once per effective destination and can be reused from a peer.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The destination scan is necessary for the requested published view, is off the immediate move critical path, and coalesces with an existing peer anchor.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use a published default-chat custom agent from a peer whose own folder does not contain it
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Snapshot construction first settles the peer anchor. If the selected agent is absent, it also reads the published anchor's applied plugins before SDK launch/restart can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Settle Copilot customization discovery for the published anchor if it has never been read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero boundary calls when the published picker anchor is warm; otherwise one cold anchor discovery shared session-wide.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The peer used the session-wide snapshot directly, so no second anchor lookup was needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A peer launch/restart selecting the fallback agent waits for the published snapshot.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The fallback adds at most one published-anchor lookup per snapshot requiring cross-anchor agent fallback, independent of total chats. Plugin projection scales with the customization lists in the peer and published anchors.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The published lookup awaits the same shared anchor promise; concurrent users coalesce discovery rather than launch separate scans.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The published anchor is refcounted and normally already warm because it supplies the session's picker. If cold, one discovery initializes it for all users. Only the selected agent is appended; no additional retained anchor is created beyond the published reference.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the fallback call flow, but low evidence of meaningful repeated cost because the published anchor and its settled promise are shared.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A cold published anchor during fallback is uncommon because the picker view generally initializes it first; customization-list sizes vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The fallback lookup is bounded to one shared anchor and is required to resolve an agent exposed by the picker.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dispose peers, replace runtimes, or finalize a session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Disposal releases the chat's anchor reference; replacement acquires the next entry before releasing the previous one so a shared discovery is not torn down mid-restart. Session finalization disposes every remaining anchor and watcher.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose customization and MCP filesystem watchers owned by released anchors/roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per anchor/root when its last reference is released; once for each remaining live anchor at session finalization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One session discovery was disposed; the PR adds multiple refcounted anchors but also explicit last-user and final-session cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous cleanup is proportional to live anchors but contains no scans or remote calls.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cleanup is linear in live effective anchor sets and their owned discovery objects. The real-path map is session-scoped and dies with the controller.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reference release is synchronous. Restart paths hold a temporary reference across destruction/creation, preventing rediscovery races; final disposal iterates anchors once.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Anchors are removed at refcount zero, positive caches do not outlive their last chat except the published reference, and controller disposal clears all remaining anchors. MCP root discoveries have their own refcounts and release watchers at zero.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from explicit reference ownership, replacement ordering, and finalizer code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Watcher-disposal implementation cost depends on the file provider, but live anchor count is bounded by active folder sets and cleanup has no evidenced expensive asynchronous boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No cleanup-lifecycle finding. The diff retains handles through replacement and deterministically releases every discovery/watch set.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and all diff pages. Traced cold/warm creation, peer fan-out, default-chat moves, selected-agent fallback, sends, restarts, and teardown through SDK IPC, filesystem discovery/watchers, MCP reads, realpath normalization, and metadata access. The PR increases cold discovery from one session anchor to one distinct folder set, but this is the authoritative work required for per-chat folder correctness, is normalized/refcounted/coalesced, remains warm across sends, shares MCP roots separately, and cleans up at last use. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
